analysis.title: Splash Zone: Hedge Funds Go Underweight AI For First Time Since 2023 As Record De-Grossing Meets Record-Low Correlation
key_insights: Hedge funds moved underweight the broader AI trade for the first time since early 2023. Combined summer and October de-grossing is the largest sustained stretch of L/S fund de-risking in over 15 years, per MS (Savone).

MS Prime Brokerage: cumulative gross flow is down 8% from the June peak. This week's buying was mostly short covering, which lifted US L/S net leverage 5 points to 51% while gross slipped 1 point to 207%.

On Thursday the S&P 500 fell while more than 80% of stocks advanced. MS says this is the first time in its data history (nearly 40 years) and the strongest positive breadth on an S&P down day since at least 1990. Dispersion was in the 88th percentile of its five-year range.

Single-name vol relative to index vol is at a record high (data back to 2005), and six-month pairwise correlation of S&P stocks fell to a record low below 10%. MS QDS (Goldsmith) says dispersion is driven more by sectors, factors and themes than by single stocks.
Equal-weight S&P (RSP) is up about 15% YTD versus about 13% for the SPX and about 6% for the Mag 7. The RSP/NDX ratio is testing a downtrend in place since May 2023.

Q3 earnings: 80% of S&P companies beat on EPS and 69% beat on sales, with a 2.8% median EPS surprise that offered limited support for positive revisions. Blended Q3 EPS growth of 30% is carried mainly by Energy (+143%) and Info Tech (+65%). Health Care is negative.

Hyperscaler results disappointed on specific parts. Microsoft revenue rose 19% YoY to $92.3B with Azure up 48% in constant currency and next-quarter guidance of 49-50%. Alphabet Search growth slowed to 12% versus about 14% expected despite 103% Google Cloud growth. AWS grew 39%, below elevated expectations, against about $220B of planned 2026 capex.

Intel fell nearly 29%, its worst day since 1974, after guiding 4Q revenue down 6% sequentially versus 4% growth expected. ServiceNow guided 4Q cRPO growth to 18.5% versus about 20% expected, with NOW down 27% and FTNT down 20% (Fortinet fell 21% on weaker services revenue).

MS's Wilson says the mid-cycle correction is entering its final stages. His three clearing events are AI financing concerns, the midterm elections, and tighter financial conditions from Fed policy and higher energy prices. He expects semiconductor weakness to find support around mid-November, potentially after another 10-15% decline, and keeps an 8,000 year-end S&P base case.

Fed chair Warsh held at 3.75-4.0%. MS economist Gapen expects 25bp hikes in December and March to 4.25-4.5%. Yields fell after the hold, which Savone questions as either inflation confidence or growth concern.

Prediction markets price 66% odds of a Democratic sweep. MS says a Democratic win in any of NC-03, FL-07, FL-13 or VA-05 implies 97% odds of a wave election. A Democratic sweep brings expectations of more durable restrictions on data centers.

MS estimates scheduled SNAP and Medicaid cuts would subtract 20bps from 2027 real consumption growth, with the baseline slowing from 2.5% to 2.0%. A Democratic sweep would lift 2027 growth by 0.1pp to 2.1%.
Brazil: Lula won with 51.8% of the vote against 80-95% priced odds of a Flavio Bolsonaro win. MS's Machado sees USD/BRL potentially testing 5.50, then moving toward 5.60-5.70.

Asia: KOSPI fell 3.5%, SK Hynix fell 7.1%, Taiwan fell 2.5% and the Nikkei fell 2.1%. KOSPI drawdown since late September is about 16-17%. Kioxia ADR fell 17% on a weak December-quarter outlook. CSI1000 fell 8.5% WTD, and MS says the National Team bought US$15B of equities during October 9-20.

Europe: Fitch cut France's outlook to negative. European gas briefly exceeded €100/MWh for the first time since 2022, with storage at 74.9%. MS's Zavolock sees recovery leadership in Semis, Tech Hardware, Cap Goods, Metals & Mining and Banks, with Top Picks Nokia, ASML and ABN AMRO.

Power is the one AI trade still working. MS's Byrd raised global power consumption estimates 10% to about 36 trillion units by 2030 and sees a net US power shortfall of 38GW through 2028. MS expects global data center capacity to grow by 180GW (23% a year) from 2026 to 2030.

Other MS views: BoJ expected to hike to 1.50% in December and 1.75% in March. German defense outlays seen reaching €1.2 trillion through 2035. MS cross-asset (Tang) keeps an overweight in global equities versus fixed income, citing $1.6 trillion of projected 2027 AI capex.

earnings_insights: S&P Q3 season (reported, per MS): 80% beat on EPS, 69% beat on sales, median EPS surprise 2.8%, blended Q3 EPS growth 30%. 44.5% of S&P market cap has reported and 13.2% reports next week.
Microsoft (reported): revenue $92.3B, up 19% YoY. Azure grew 48% in constant currency, up 6 points. Guidance for next-quarter Azure growth is 49-50%.
Alphabet (reported): Google Cloud grew 103%. Search grew 12% versus about 14% expected, and trailed Meta ad growth by about 13 points per MS's Nowak.
Amazon (reported): AWS grew 39%, below elevated expectations. Planned 2026 capex is about $220B. The text for the backlog and QoQ figures is garbled in the source.
Intel (guidance): 4Q revenue seen down 6% sequentially versus 4% growth expected. 2027 flagged as an investment year without positive FCF.
ServiceNow (guidance): 4Q cRPO growth 18.5% versus about 20% expected. AI ACV target raised to $1.7B from $1.5B.
Reddit (reported): revenue missed buy-side expectations of roughly $950M. US DAUs fell by 900K. The reported revenue figure is garbled in the source.
Fortinet (reported): fell 21% on weaker services revenue.

Funds covered index hedges and added Tech (Memory, Agentic AI, Internet, Cybersecurity) while selling Hyperscalers, Energy, Materials and Real Estate.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is already considerably lighter, the de-grossing is the largest on record, and the average stock is doing fine. Wilson sees the correction entering its final stages and Tang keeps an overweight in global equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Earnings expectations are not stabilizing with growth peaking, AI financing concerns persist, the Fed is hiking, and Wilson wants another 10-15% decline in semis. The sentiment indicator is only at neutral.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Semiconductors failing to find support around mid-November after another 10-15% decline, or the MS Sentiment Indicator moving to capitulation extremes without recovery.

tension_points.bull_case: A Republican win (8% odds) is status quo with an OBBBA tailwind.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic sweep (65%) brings regime uncertainty and expectations of more durable restrictions on data centers. A narrow Democratic win (29%) is the most fiscally restrictive and carries brinksmanship risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic win in any of NC-03, FL-07, FL-13 or VA-05, which implies 97% odds of a wave election.
